item_title: Both released on schedule: Q2 GDP advance estimate +1.5% annualized, June PCE inflation exactly at consensus (headline +3.7% YoY, core +3.3% YoY)
mechanism: Soft growth alongside inflation that hasn't cooled narrows the Fed's room to cut, which typically supports the dollar and pressures capital toward US assets even as growth itself softens.

scenarios.direction: The Fed holds its hawkish line, the dollar stays firm, and EM capital outflows continue on the yield advantage.
scenarios.why: A central bank on hold with above-target inflation has historically kept real rates attractive relative to peers, pulling portfolio flows toward the anchor currency.
scenarios.precedent: The Fed's 2022 hiking cycle, held against still-sticky inflation, produced sustained dollar strength (DXY +15% that year) and visible EM outflow pressure, especially in currencies with dollar-denominated debt.

scenarios.direction: Growth softness dominates pricing over the next few prints instead, pulling rate-cut expectations forward despite today's hawkish hold.
scenarios.why: Markets often re-price toward growth risk once a soft print repeats, overriding a central bank's stated inflation focus if the labor/spending data turns further.

context_note: Lands on top of an already-elevated geopolitical risk premium from the widening Iran conflict (see World News), which independently pressures the same safe-asset demand this print is testing.

item_title: Amazon reported: net sales $200.6B (+20% YoY), AWS $42.2B (+37% YoY — fastest in 18 quarters), AWS operating income $16.6B (+64% YoY), property/equipment purchases up $66.1B YoY.
mechanism: Amazon's AWS beat is the second hyperscaler print, after Microsoft, showing AI capex converting into accelerating cloud revenue rather than just backlog.

scenarios.direction: Capital markets keep rewarding hyperscalers that show real revenue conversion, funding further capex rounds.
scenarios.why: Two consecutive confirmed conversions in one week (Azure +43%, AWS +37%) give the bull case a harder floor than backlog claims alone.
scenarios.precedent: Microsoft's 07-29 report showed the same pattern one day earlier: Azure crossing $100B run-rate at +41% growth drove an immediate +9% stock reaction, the week's first instance of this conversion-reward pattern.

scenarios.direction: The bar keeps rising each quarter, so today's beat becomes next quarter's baseline and eventually disappoints.
scenarios.why: Markets that reward acceleration typically require the acceleration to continue, not just repeat, or an equal beat reads as deceleration.

context_note: Reinforces rather than complicates the GDP/PCE read: this growth traces to real enterprise cloud demand, not just capex accounting.
